steps.tail:
Install the browser once with `npx playwright install chromium`. Only Playwright and `@axe-core/playwright` were added as direct dependencies. Run the checker's integration tests with `node --test check.test.mjs`.

The supplied workspace has **no design or content reference**. The checker intentionally fails the dependent checks. It does not generate its expectations from the implementation. Supply these independently reviewed inputs to make those checks executable:

- `check-design.json`: an object with `sections` (a nonempty array of `{ "name": "…", "selector": "…" }` in design order) and `colors` (a nonempty array of exact `#RRGGBB` colours from the design). Selectors must uniquely identify the rendered sections. Both DOM order and top-to-bottom/left-to-right visual order are checked.
- `content.txt`: verbatim text, split into pieces by blank lines. Alternatively `content.json`: nested arrays/objects with text string leaves; every leaf is required. JSON takes precedence if both exist. Only whitespace is normalized; case and punctuation are exact. Keep metadata and URLs that are not intended as visible copy out of this text-only reference.

The target is the root page of this static Astro site. Browser checks run at widths 390, 768 and 1440, height 900, device scale 1, dark colour preference, reduced motion, English locale and UTC. Each width gets a fresh context. Entire vertical screenshots and reachable keyboard focus states are checked. The suite does not claim to exercise arbitrary click-driven application states or other routes.

Colour matching is deliberately literal: every captured RGB pixel must occur in the reference palette. No rounding, nearest-colour matching, antialiasing exceptions or image exemptions are used. Consequently text smoothing, transparency, shadows and photographs can fail even if their CSS source colours match the design. Reports group unexpected colours by the element hit-tested at their pixel coordinates; coordinates are document CSS pixels. Overlapping or pointer-events-disabled layers can make the hit-test name refer to an underlying element. Do not expand the design palette from observed screenshots merely to make it pass.

The check has bounded execution and capture limits; exceeding them fails. Keep package-lock.json and the Playwright browser version fixed for reproducible rendering. Dynamic or externally changing page content may itself be nondeterministic; this checker uses no model, random sampling or human decisions.
